disposition: BLOCKED: browser SSO identity transport is not established; retained Chromium evidence demonstrates host-only cookie is absent on other-destination proxy requests

workflow.browser_step: Real Chromium: where does the browser send the portal session cookie?

browser_fixture.binding_limit: Browser file hash independently derived from exact workflow checkout; artifact binding.txt records Go fixture hash, not browser hash. Browser fixture itself does not load the candidate application.

source_fixture_results.fixed: PASS: callback302/portal cookie; identical response replay401/no cookie;8 cookie-purpose controls
source_fixture_results.limitation: Go HTTP client manually attaches signed cookie to proxy request; this does not model browser destination-cookie selection.

browser_results.result: PASS for browser cookie-scope demonstration; not PASS for Culvert SSO traffic
browser_results.mechanism: Real Chromium stores a synthetic host-only HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie from a Node recording forward proxy acting as ui.test, follows a redirect to dest.test, browses HTTP dest.test and returns to ui.test, then attempts HTTPS CONNECT. No cookie header is manually injected into Chromium requests.

finding.priority: P1 functional release blocker for advertised browser SSO proxy traffic
finding.status: Source-backed, browser-cookie behavior reproduced in retained CI; complete application browser flow not independently run
finding.trigger: Browser completes SAML or OIDC at the UI origin, then accesses a different origin through the explicit proxy without separate Basic credentials.
finding.cause: setSessionCookie creates a host-only UI cookie. resolveRequestAuth reads the destination request Cookie for SSO identity; no cookie means it takes no-credential handling. Chromium does not attach the UI cookie to unrelated HTTP destinations or their CONNECT request.
finding.impact: SSO login cannot by itself establish identity for ordinary different-origin proxy traffic. Depending on configured policy the request is challenged/redirected or treated as unauthenticated, rather than using the signed-in user identity. This is a functional identity-transport gap, not evidence of a cookie leak or authorization bypass.
finding.applies_to: Both SAML and OIDC issuance through shared setSessionCookie; only synthetic SAML handler flow was exercised in source fixture.
finding.minimum_closure: Select a supported browser-to-proxy authentication transport; exercise actual browser login through real Culvert, then HTTP and HTTPS/CONNECT to distinct destinations and verify the authenticated subject/groups and policy allow/deny behavior. Do not establish closure by manually adding Cookie headers or simply broadening cookie scope to destination origins.

alternate_flow_review.callbacks: ui_auth.go:974 and ui_auth.go:1007 call setSessionCookie, then redirect. Full success paths inspected: no post-login IP/session cache registration or Proxy-Authorization issuance.
alternate_flow_review.resolution: proxy.go:355 reads the signed Cookie, proxy.go:372 parses separate Proxy-Authorization Basic credentials; then no-credential resolution redirects/challenges/denies. Full resolveRequestAuth inspected; no IP-to-SSO-principal fallback.
alternate_flow_review.lookup_search: No ClientSessionGate, AuthenticateByIP, sessionByIP, byClientIP or ipToIdentity matches in exact product production Go source. Broader IP/session/principal search did not identify callback-to-proxy binding.
alternate_flow_review.qualification: This supports the source inference for browser-only login without separately configured proxy credentials; it is not a full live application-browser reproduction.

limitations: No Culvert process, genuine SAML assertion or actual IdP in the Chromium script; its cookie is a synthetic fixed value.
Recording proxy terminates CONNECT with502; no TLS tunnel or HTTPS destination content is loaded. It still records that actual CONNECT request lacks the UI cookie.
The synthetic cookie is plain HTTP without Secure; production Secure flag is dynamic. The fixture proves destination scoping, not TLS cookie behavior.

Browser script allows expected navigation failure and broadly ignores uncaught exceptions; recorded successful UI control and three destination requests support the bounded observation, not a general browser reliability claim.
No exact Chromium version retained in the tiny artifacts.
No new tests, OVA import, endpoint calls or VM actions performed in this audit.
remaining: Browser-bound SAML/OIDC state (login-CSRF) remains open; this cookie-scope exercise does not address it.

Exact adopted-sidecar scan and replacement appliance qualification are outside this two-artifact run. Parent separately reported a replacement OVA artifact appearing; that builder is not audited here.
No conclusions transferred from the historical cd8 ESXi lifecycle to the new candidate.
next_esxi_target: 2a may be used as a clearly labeled diagnostic candidate; the callback fix and successful source fixture do not close browser SSO or justify production-ready signoff. Record IdP/browser identity transport as BLOCKED until the supported complete flow passes.
